name: Panasonic-fk
title: FK series surface-mount aluminum electrolytic capacitors, 105 °C, low impedance
summary: FK is a family of polarised aluminum electrolytic chip capacitors: a round can standing on a base plate with two flat terminals, soldered by reflow. Ratings cover 6.3 V to 100 V and 3.3 µF to 6800 µF in cans from 4 mm to 18 mm across, rated for 2000 h at 105 °C (5000 h for 12.5 mm and wider cans and the G-suffix 8 × 10.2 and 10 × 10.2 parts). Each rating carries a maximum impedance at 100 kHz and a ripple-current rating; many come in a vibration-proof build with extra support terminals, and the series is AEC-Q200 qualified.

operation.text: Black ink on the can top: capacitance in µF, the series mark FK, a voltage code letter, a lot number, a black dot for lead-free, and a bar over the negative side. Cans up to ø10 and from ø12.5 carry the same items in slightly different layouts.

Cans of ø10 and larger have a vent in the top. When it opens it releases electrolyte vapour hotter than 100 °C; keep high-current or high-voltage traces from running above it and leave free space over it (2 mm for 6.3 to 16 mm cans, 3 mm for 18 mm).

Available from ø6.3 up, ordered with a V in the last place of the part number. Its dimensions differ from the standard build, and it has support terminals that solder to arms on the land; it is rated to 30 G sine vibration, 5 Hz to 2000 Hz. On ø6.3 parts the support terminals wrap from the underside to the plate edge; their underside joint gives the vibration rating even when no side fillet forms.

The part is polarised; reverse voltage is not allowed. DC bias plus ripple peak must stay at or below the rated voltage, and the ripple must not drive the part into reverse. Keep ripple at or below its rated value. Inrush current must stay under 100 A, and more than 10 000 power cycles per day, or fast repeated charge and discharge, calls for the conditions to be given to Panasonic first.
Paralleled capacitors should share one part number and see balanced wiring so ripple does not crowd into one of them. Series connection is not allowed.

Heat raises leakage current. Cold lowers capacitance and raises tan δ and impedance. Higher frequency lowers capacitance and impedance and raises tan δ; low frequency raises ESR and so the heating from ripple.

The aluminium case has bare, uninsulated metal; keep it isolated from the cathode terminal and from board copper, and do not touch it in a live circuit. The marked sleeve is not guaranteed to insulate.
On a double-sided board, run no traces directly under the part, where leaked electrolyte could bridge them.

Reflow only (infrared or hot air); no flow or dip soldering. A second reflow waits until the part is back at room temperature. Vapour-phase reflow should ramp at 3 °C/s or less. Hand soldering: 350 °C for no more than 3 s. Curing ovens: 150 °C for 2 min at most. Measure part temperature with a thermocouple glued to the can top.

Withstands immersion or ultrasonic cleaning at 60 °C or below for under 5 minutes, followed by rinsing and forced drying. Pine Alpha ST-100S and Cleanthrough 750H/750L/710M are qualified. Flux in the bath at 2 % mass or less. Avoid halogenated solvents (1,1,1-trichloroethane above all), alkaline or petroleum solvents, xylene and acetone. Adhesives and coatings should use non-halogen solvents, no chloroprene polymer, and leave at least a third of the seal uncovered; no potting.
A charge can reappear across the terminals; discharge through about 1 kΩ. After long storage leakage rises; bring the voltage up through about 1 kΩ.
Storage period is 42 months from the shipping inspection, at 5 °C to 35 °C and 45 % to 85 % relative humidity, out of direct sunlight.
